decision_rules: 1070 nm is a hard target: a 1064-nm value is neighboring-wavelength evidence, not an exact 1070-nm value.
Preserve whether a source reports mus or musp; derive one from the other only when the same source supplies or explicitly assumes g.
Convert inverse-length coefficients from cm^-1 to mm^-1 by dividing by 10 and record the conversion.
Do not average conflicting sources by default; retain them as discrete sensitivity candidates until a documented selection is reviewed.
Simulation assumptions such as fixed g or n are not measurements and cannot be relabeled as direct data.
A production row stays TBD until mua, mus or musp plus g, and n are all resolved for the atlas tissue definition.

coverage.blocking_reason: A boundary-medium convention is identified, but it has not been frozen with the production optical scenario.
Human CSF transmission supports a water proxy and numeric water mua/n candidates now exist, but physiological CSF scattering and anisotropy remain unmeasured and the proxy requires explicit review.
Exact Table S1 coefficients are transcribed, but they come from one frozen cadaver and an inversion with fixed g and n; nominal selection and sensitivity review remain open.
Exact Shapey coefficients are transcribed, but fixed g conflicts with other brain assumptions and the independent Yaroslavsky white-matter transcription remains unresolved.
A human adipose scattering model and digitized 1070-nm absorption estimate exist, but absorption has a material method conflict, g was fixed, and n is unresolved.

Exact porcine-muscle and bulk in-vivo human upper-arm coefficients plus a 20-nm extrapolated human SCM reduced-scattering model are available, but none is an isolated-human complete tuple and g/n remain unresolved.
This atlas class is composite; pure-skin, muscle, and bulk-forehead measurements require discrete proxy cases because the source supplies no composition fraction.
Digitized intact-cranial absorption and a cortical-skull scattering model now exist, but bone-site/preparation conflicts, fixed g, and unresolved n prevent a nominal choice.
The atlas distinction between fat and fat_2 is not defined by the optical literature; absorption and n also remain unresolved.
Exact human-dura coefficients are transcribed, but the data are single-cadaver ex vivo values, g and n were fixed inputs, and the older scattering model remains only secondarily verified.
Exact human frozen tibial-marrow coefficients are available but have boundary effects and do not establish cranial applicability, g, or n.
Primary hct-42.1 and hct-33.2 graph-derived 1070-nm candidates now cover absorption and scattering state sensitivities, but n and atlas lumen/wall or arterial/venous mapping remain unresolved.
